title: How to customize cursor in Cursor on Mac: a complete guide for developers
metaTitle: How to customize cursor in Cursor on Mac
description: Learn how to customize the text cursor in the Cursor editor on Mac and adjust your system pointer settings for a better coding experience.
intro: To customize the text cursor in the Cursor editor on Mac, you must access the User Settings menu within the application. If you want to change the system-wide mouse pointer, you need to adjust the settings in your macOS System Settings.
tldr: Open the Command Palette with ⌘ ⇧ P.
Search for Preferences: Open User Settings (UI).
Find the Cursor section to adjust style, width, and blinking.
Use macOS System Settings to change the system mouse pointer.
Edit settings.json for advanced control over cursor appearance.

blocks.text: Understanding the two types of cursors

When you look to customize cursor on Mac, you are likely dealing with two distinct interfaces. First, there is the text editor cursor. This is the blinking line inside your code files. Second, there is the system pointer. This is the arrow or hand icon that you move around your screen to click buttons and select files.

The Cursor editor is a fork of VS Code. This means it inherits the exact same configuration system. You can change how your text cursor behaves, looks, and moves by using the internal settings of the application. The system pointer, however, is controlled by macOS itself. Changing one does not affect the other.
How to change the text cursor style in Cursor
You can modify your text cursor appearance through the user interface. This is the safest way to experiment with different styles without touching raw code files.

items: Open your Cursor editor on your Mac.
Press ⌘ ⇧ P to open the Command Palette.
Type Preferences: Open User Settings (UI) and press Return.
Type cursor into the search bar at the top of the settings page.
Locate the Editor: Cursor Style section and select your preferred shape from the dropdown menu.
Adjust the Editor: Cursor Blinking setting to match your preference for focus.
Change the Editor: Cursor Width setting if you want a thicker or thinner insertion point.

blocks.text: The available styles include block, block-outline, line, line-thin, underline, and underline-thin. Many developers prefer the block style for better visibility when working with dark themes. If you find the blinking distracting, try setting it to solid.
If you want more granular control, you can edit the settings.json file directly. This method allows you to copy and paste configurations between different machines or projects.

items: Open the Command Palette with ⌘ ⇧ P.
Search for Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON) and press Return.
Add or update the following keys to your configuration object:
"editor.cursorStyle": "line",
"editor.cursorBlinking": "smooth",
"editor.cursorWidth": 2
Save the file with ⌘ S to apply the changes immediately.

blocks.text: Always ensure your JSON syntax is valid. Missing a comma or a closing brace will prevent the settings from loading. If you notice your changes are not taking effect, check the bottom status bar for any error messages.
Customizing the system mouse pointer on Mac
If you want to change the size or color of your system-wide mouse pointer, you must use the macOS System Settings. This changes the look of the cursor across all applications, including Cursor.

items: Click the Apple menu in the top left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings.
Navigate to Accessibility in the sidebar.
Click on Display.
Use the Pointer size slider to make your cursor larger.
Click on the color wells for Pointer outline color and Pointer fill color to change the cursor appearance.
Click Reset Colors if you want to revert to the default white and black scheme.

blocks.text: Note that macOS does not allow you to change the cursor shape to custom icons natively. If you want to use a custom pointer, you will need to install third-party software like Mousecape. These tools are separate from the Cursor editor and macOS system defaults.

Users often struggle with finding the right setting because the search bar in the settings menu is sometimes too broad. If you cannot find the cursor settings, make sure you are in the User tab rather than the Workspace tab. Workspace settings override User settings, which can be confusing if you have specific configurations for different projects.

Another common issue is thinking that changing the cursor style will change the mouse pointer. Remember that the text cursor is strictly for writing code, while the pointer is for navigating the interface. If you are struggling to see your cursor, consider increasing the cursor width rather than changing the style.

faq.question: Can I use custom cursor icons in Cursor?
faq.answer: No, the Cursor editor does not support custom image files for the text cursor. You are limited to the styles provided in the settings, such as block, line, or underline.

faq.question: Does changing the cursor in VS Code affect Cursor?
faq.answer: Cursor is a fork of VS Code, so it shares the same configuration structure. If you sync your settings, your cursor preferences will likely carry over.

faq.question: Why does my cursor disappear in dark mode?
faq.answer: This is usually a theme issue rather than a cursor setting issue. Check your color theme settings or ensure your cursor color is set to a high-contrast value in your JSON configuration.
